{{Short description|American mathematician}}
'''James Haglund''' is an American mathematician who specializes in [[algebraic combinatorics]] and [[enumerative combinatorics]],<ref>[https://www2.math.upenn.edu/~jhaglund James Haglund's Home Page]</ref> and works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>[https://www.math.upenn.edu/people/james-haglund James Haglund] at [https://www.math.upenn.edu Penn Math Dept]</ref>

==Education==
Haglund received his Ph.D. in 1993 from the [[University of Georgia]], with the dissertation ''Compositions, Rook Placements, and Permutations of Vectors'' supervised by Earl Rodney Canfield.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|5627}}</ref>

==Research contributions==
In 2005, together with [[Mark Haiman|M. Haiman]] and N. Loehr gave the first proof of a combinatorial interpretation of the Macdonald polynomials. In 2007, Haglund, Haiman and Loehr gave a combinatorial formula for the non-symmetric [[Macdonald polynomials]].

Haglund is the author of ''The <math>q,t</math>-Catalan Numbers and the Space of Diagonal Harmonics: With an Appendix on the Combinatorics of Macdonald Polynomials''.<ref>[''The <math>q,t</math>-Catalan Numbers and the Space of Diagonal Harmonics: With an Appendix on the Combinatorics of Macdonald Polynomials''], University Lecture Series, vol. 41, American Mathematical Society, 2008. Reviews: Michael A. Zabrocki (2009), {{MR|2371044}}; Pavlo Pylyavskyy, {{zbl|1142.05074}}</ref>

==Academic talks==
In 2024, Haglund gave a talk at [[KAIST]] on  Superization of Symmetric Functions.<ref>[https://kaist.combinatorics.kr/2024-05 KAIST Combinatorics Lab]</ref>

In 2015, together with [[Alexandre Kirillov]] and [[Ching-Li Chai]], Haglund gave a talk at [https://pwcc.upenn.edu/ Penn Wharton China Center] on Penn Math Day, sponsored by the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and [[Peking University]].<ref>[https://www2.math.upenn.edu/~jhaglund/talks/PWCCposter.pdf Penn Math Day]</ref>

In 2006, he gave a Plenary Address at the 18th [[International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics]] ([[FPSAC]] '06), San Diego (USA).<ref>[https://fpsac.org/confs/fpsac-2006/ FPSAC'06: San Diego]</ref>

==Editorial==
Haglund was on the editorial boards of [[Transactions of the AMS]], Journal of Combinatorics, and a few other academic journals.

==Students==
Among the Ph.D. students supervised by Haglund are [https://www.ycp.edu/faculty-staff-directory/frederick-butler Frederick M. Butler], [[Mahir Bilen Can]], [https://sites.google.com/site/ltcrewmath/ Logan Crew], [https://sites.google.com/wfu.edu/sarahmason/ Sarah Katherine Mason], [https://baruch.cuny.edu/profiles/faculty/Anna-Pun Anna Pun], [[Chunwei Song]], and [https://meesue.github.io Meesue Yoo].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|5627}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2013, Haglund became an inaugural Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>
